title: Why Your Favorite Vegetables Are Disappearing from British Gardens
subtitle: As record-breaking heat changes the UK climate, gardeners are being forced to rethink what they grow for dinner.

summary.en: The United Kingdom recently experienced its hottest summer on record, leading to significant challenges for agriculture. The Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) now advises home gardeners to stop growing cauliflower and other similar vegetables. These plants struggle to grow in high temperatures and require too much water. Experts suggest that gardeners should switch to heat-loving crops like tomatoes, peppers, and even melons. This shift reflects a broader change in how people must adapt to a warming climate.
summary.zh: 英國近期經歷了有紀錄以來最炎熱的夏天，導致農業面臨重大挑戰。英國皇家園藝學會（RHS）現建議家庭園丁停止種植花椰菜及其他類似蔬菜。這些植物在高溫下難以生長且需要大量水分。專家建議園丁應改種番茄、辣椒甚至甜瓜等喜熱作物。這種轉變反映了人們在面對氣候暖化時，必須進行更廣泛的適應與調整。

paragraphs.en: The traditional British Sunday roast is facing an unexpected problem: the cauliflower is disappearing from gardens across the country. Following a summer of record-breaking heat, the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) has officially recommended that home gardeners stop trying to grow cauliflower and other related vegetables, known as brassicas. This group of plants includes broccoli, cabbages, and brussels sprouts, which have long been staples in British vegetable patches.
paragraphs.zh: 傳統的英式週日烤肉正面臨一個意想不到的問題：花椰菜正在全國各地的花園中消失。在經歷了破紀錄的炎熱夏季後，英國皇家園藝學會（Royal Horticultural Society, RHS）正式建議家庭園丁停止種植花椰菜及其他相關蔬菜，這些蔬菜統稱為十字花科植物。這類植物包括花椰菜、高麗菜和抱子甘藍，長期以來一直是英國菜園裡的主要作物。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, this change is a direct result of the UK’s shifting climate. This past summer was the hottest on record, with temperatures in London reaching 38.1C in August. June was also confirmed as the hottest June since records began in 1884. Scientists have linked these intense heatwaves to the climate crisis, which is largely caused by the burning of fossil fuels—the coal, oil, and gas used to create energy. Because these vegetables are “thirsty” and easily stressed by high heat, they often fail to grow properly, leaving gardeners with very little to harvest.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，這種變化是英國氣候變遷的直接結果。剛過去的夏天是有紀錄以來最熱的一個夏天，八月份倫敦氣溫達到攝氏三十八點一度。六月也被證實是自一八八四年有紀錄以來最熱的六月。科學家將這些強烈的熱浪與氣候危機連結起來，而這場危機主要是由燃燒化石燃料（即用於產生能源的煤炭、石油和天然氣）所引起。由於這些蔬菜非常「渴水」且容易因高溫而產生壓力，它們往往無法正常生長，導致園丁幾乎沒有收成。

paragraphs.en: Guy Barter, the chief horticulturist at the RHS, explained that cauliflowers have been the hardest hit of all common garden vegetables. He noted that as summers continue to follow these hot patterns, gardeners should choose different plants that are more likely to succeed. “Swapping them out for an equally flavourful and nutritious alternative will save on all-important watering and provide a better guarantee of a good harvest,” Barter said. The charity suggests that gardeners focus on crops that can handle the heat, such as tomatoes, peppers, and even melons, which can now grow outdoors in some parts of the UK.
paragraphs.zh: 英國皇家園藝學會的首席園藝師蓋伊·巴特（Guy Barter）解釋說，在所有常見的庭園蔬菜中，花椰菜受到的打擊最為嚴重。他指出，隨著夏季持續出現這種高溫模式，園丁應該選擇更有可能成功的不同植物。巴特表示：「將它們替換成同樣美味且營養豐富的替代作物，不僅能節省極為重要的澆灌用水，還能更有保障地獲得豐收。」該慈善機構建議園丁將重心放在耐熱作物上，例如番茄、辣椒，甚至是現在已能在英國部分地區戶外種植的甜瓜。

paragraphs.en: For many gardeners, this advice confirms what they have already experienced. Simone Bratt, who manages the kitchen gardens at RHS Bridgewater, said she stopped growing cauliflower several years ago. She explained that the growth was very inconsistent due to extreme weather. Even when they tried planting in the spring, the heat was too much for the plants. “They bolted before we even got them in the ground,” she said, referring to the way plants grow too quickly and produce flowers instead of the vegetable head when they are stressed. Bratt suggests that gardeners try purple sprouting broccoli instead, as it is a more reliable crop that can be harvested over a longer period.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多園丁來說，這項建議證實了他們早已有的經驗。負責管理皇家園藝學會布里奇沃特花園（RHS Bridgewater）廚房花園的西蒙娜·布拉特（Simone Bratt）表示，她幾年前就停止種植花椰菜了。她解釋說，由於極端天氣，作物的生長非常不穩定。即使他們嘗試在春天種植，高溫對植物來說也太過強烈。她說：「我們甚至還沒把它們種進土裡，它們就已經抽苔了。」她指的是植物在受到壓力時，會生長過快並開花，而不是長出蔬菜花球。布拉特建議園丁改種紫芽花椰菜，因為這是一種更可靠的作物，可以收成的時間也更長。

paragraphs.en: Other experts are also finding success with different types of plants. Liz Mooney, a horticulturist at RHS Garden Wisley, noted that she has moved her focus entirely to “warmth-loving crops.” Some gardeners are now successfully growing cucumbers and sweet potatoes outdoors. Others have turned to kale, which is a hardy plant that often grows back year after year. Because kale has deeper roots, it is better at surviving during times of drought—a long period without enough rain.
paragraphs.zh: 其他專家也在嘗試不同類型的植物並獲得成功。皇家園藝學會威斯利花園（RHS Garden Wisley）的園藝師莉茲·穆尼（Liz Mooney）指出，她已將重心完全轉向「喜溫作物」。有些園丁現在已能成功在戶外種植小黃瓜和地瓜。其他人則轉向種植羽衣甘藍，這是一種耐寒且通常能年復一年再生的植物。由於羽衣甘藍的根系較深，在乾旱（即長期缺乏足夠雨水的時期）期間，它能更好地存活。

paragraphs.en: This shift in gardening habits is not just about personal preference; it is a necessary response to a changing environment. While the RHS hopes that recent rains might help winter crops like carrots and leeks recover this year, the long-term outlook suggests that British gardens will look very different in the future. As the climate continues to warm, the ability to adapt by choosing the right plants will be essential for anyone wanting to grow their own food. For now, the cauliflower remains a difficult challenge for even the most experienced gardeners, marking a clear end to its time as a reliable garden favorite.
paragraphs.zh: 這種園藝習慣的轉變不僅僅是個人偏好，更是對環境變遷的必要回應。雖然皇家園藝學會希望近期的降雨能幫助胡蘿蔔和韭蔥等冬季作物在今年恢復生長，但長期來看，英國的花園在未來將會呈現截然不同的樣貌。隨著氣候持續暖化，對於任何想要自行種植食物的人來說，透過選擇合適的植物來適應環境將變得至關重要。目前，花椰菜對即使是最有經驗的園丁來說，依然是一項艱鉅的挑戰，這也明確標誌著它作為可靠庭園寵兒的時代已經結束。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Important or main products that are regularly used or produced.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（訂書針），這裡指日常生活中不可或缺的農作物。文中：This group of plants includes broccoli, cabbages, and brussels sprouts, which have long been staples in British vegetable patches.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To grow too quickly and produce flowers instead of the edible part of the plant.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（衝出、逃跑），這裡指植物因壓力而過早開花。文中：They bolted before we even got them in the ground

keyTerms.definitionEn: Strong enough to survive difficult conditions, such as extreme weather.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 耐寒的；強壯的；適應力強的。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於形容人（堅強的），這裡形容植物在惡劣環境下仍能存活。文中：Others have turned to kale, which is a hardy plant that often grows back year after year.

previousArticles.summaryEn: Recent record-breaking heatwaves in the UK have made it difficult to grow traditional vegetables like cauliflower. The Royal Horticultural Society now advises gardeners to stop planting these thirsty crops. Instead, experts suggest switching to heat-loving plants like tomatoes, okra, and melons. This shift highlights how climate change is changing our food systems and daily habits. Gardeners are now experimenting with new varieties to ensure a successful harvest despite the changing weather.

quiz.question: According to the article, why is the Royal Horticultural Society advising gardeners to stop growing brassicas?

options.A: Because these plants are susceptible to new types of garden pests.
options.B: Because they require too much water and struggle to thrive in the recent extreme summer heat.
options.C: Because the UK government has banned the cultivation of cabbages and broccoli.
options.D: Because these vegetables are no longer considered a traditional part of the British Sunday roast.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第二段明確指出，這些蔬菜（brassicas）被描述為「口渴的」（thirsty）且容易因高溫而感到壓力，導致無法正常生長。選項 A 文章未提及害蟲問題；選項 C 為錯誤資訊，文中並未提到政府禁令；選項 D 雖然提到 Sunday roast，但文章是說 cauliflower 正從餐桌的配菜中消失，而非不再被視為傳統食物。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the future of traditional British vegetable gardening?

options.A: Gardeners will likely return to growing traditional vegetables once the current heatwave ends.
options.B: The UK will soon stop importing vegetables from other countries.
options.C: Gardeners will need to prioritize plant varieties that are more resilient to heat and drought.
options.D: Growing vegetables at home will become impossible for most people in the UK.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段與最後一段，專家建議改種耐熱作物（如番茄、甜瓜），且提到適應環境對於種植食物至關重要。這暗示了未來的園藝必須轉向適應氣候變化。選項 A 與文章提到的「長期展望」（long-term outlook）矛盾；選項 B 與文章主題無關；選項 D 過於誇大，文章僅強調需改變種植的作物種類，而非完全無法種植。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'bolted' mean in the context of the plants?

options.A: To grow rapidly and produce flowers prematurely due to stress.
options.B: To be eaten quickly by garden animals or insects.
options.C: To be planted deep into the soil to protect roots from heat.
options.D: To wither and die immediately after being placed in the ground.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中括號解釋了 'bolted' 的含義，即植物在壓力下生長過快，產出花朵而非可食用的蔬菜頭（vegetable head）。選項 B、C、D 皆未準確反映文中對該詞的定義，且「bolted」在園藝學中專指植物因環境壓力而過早抽苔開花，導致品質下降。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: The Royal Horticultural Society is failing to support British gardeners.
options.B: Cauliflower is the most nutritious vegetable for British families.
options.C: Climate change is forcing British gardeners to change which crops they grow.
options.D: Extreme heat in the UK has destroyed all types of vegetable gardens.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。整篇文章的核心在於探討氣候變遷（極端高溫）如何影響英國園藝，並導致園丁必須調整種植策略以適應環境。選項 A 文中並未批評 RHS；選項 B 為個人觀點，非文章主旨；選項 D 過度推論，文章提到仍有其他作物（如番茄、甜瓜、羽衣甘藍）可以成功生長，並非「所有」種類都毀滅。
